thread:
maria: Trying to run the quickstart sample app on WSL but `redwoodctl` login is acting flaky. Followed README, did `redwoodctl init` and created a profile, yet `redwoodctl serve --local` complains 'no active profile found'.

alex: What exact commands did you run and which distro/version? Did `redwoodctl init` finish cleanly?

maria: WSL Ubuntu 22.04. Steps: `wget https://downloads.redwood.ai/ctl/latest/redwoodctl-linux-amd64.tar.gz` -> tar xzf -> `./redwoodctl init` -> selected "Create new profile" -> named it `work`. Init printed success, but `redwoodctl list-profiles` returns nothing. CLI logs: `open /home/maria/.config/redwoodctl/profiles.json: permission denied`.

sam: Sounds like a permissions issue. Did you ever run the installer or the binary with sudo? What does `echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `ls -la ~/.config/redwoodctl` show?

maria: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is empty. `ls -la ~/.config` shows `.config` owned by root. I think I mistakenly ran the tarball with sudo earlier.

alex: That'll do it. Quick fix: `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.config/redwoodctl` then re-run `redwoodctl init --profile work` or `redwoodctl login --profile work`. Also avoid putting the config on /mnt/c due to WSL mount perms.

maria: After chown, `redwoodctl login --profile work` kicks off the device-code flow but then errors with `device code poll timeout` after ~30s. I can't finish login in the browser, it hangs.

sam: Which redwoodctl version? We had a retry/poll bug in older clients where transient network hiccups caused the poll to time out prematurely. `redwoodctl version`

maria: Shows 0.12.1 (I installed the binary manually).

alex: We patched the device code polling in 0.12.3 and added a `--timeout` flag in 0.12.4. Recommend upgrading to 0.12.4. Download the tarball and replace the binary: `https://downloads.redwood.ai/ctl/0.12.4/redwoodctl-linux-amd64.tar.gz`.

maria: Can brew handle this under WSL? I used the tarball originally.

alex: Homebrew on WSL is variable. Easiest path: fetch the 0.12.4 tarball, unpack, overwrite the binary in your path, `chmod +x`. Then run `redwoodctl login --profile work --timeout 120s`. If you can't upgrade, support has a manual helper: open the device-code URL in a browser and run `redwoodctl accept --poll-token <token>` to force-accept the poll.

maria: Upgraded to 0.12.4 and retried with `--timeout 120s`. Login completed successfully. Thank you!

maria: Small follow-up: the quickstart sample still assumes a profile named `default` and errors out when none exists. That's confusing because `init` asked me to name the profile `work`.

jim: Good catch. Quickstart should either detect the last-used profile or call out how to set `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` or run `redwoodctl init --default`. I'll file a docs issue.

devex-bot: Opened issue #1453: "quickstart assumes default profile leading to onboarding friction" assigned to @jim :spiral_note_pad:

alex: I'll patch the quickstart to mention `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE`, add a WSL troubleshooting note about `~/.config` ownership, and document the `--timeout` flag. Maria, thanks for the detailed repro — saved us a support ticket. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks everyone! :heart:
